blocks.text: Breast cancer is the second most common malignancy among women in Tanzania, with an incidence of 15%. It is the second most common cause of death in women aged 45-55 years after cervical cancer. The incidence is expected to rise in recent years due to screening programs around the country and increased awareness among the general population.

blocks.text: Table 22.11: Management by Multidisciplinary care and various modalities
Management should be planned by a multidisciplinary team (MDT) including: breast surgeon, radiologist, pathologist, clinical oncologist, and radiation oncologist

blocks.text: Integrate local and systemic therapies with optimal sequencing
Complete excision of primary tumor with negative margins
Accurate staging of tumor and axillary lymph nodes for prognosis
Modified radical mastectomy (total mastectomy + axillary lymph node dissection)
Radical mastectomy (total mastectomy + pectoralis major resection + ALND)
Extended radical mastectomy (radical mastectomy + internal mammary node dissection)
Axillary lymph node dissection (levels I–II) with >10 lymph nodes sampled
Implant-based methods: expanders, saline or silicone implants
Autologous flaps: TRAM, latissimus dorsi, DIEP flap
Breast-conserving surgery only if radiotherapy is available
If radiotherapy not available → Modified radical mastectomy preferred
Palliative: fungating/bleeding tumors, bone or brain metastases
Tumor bed boost: 10 Gy in selected cases
